findings.impact: A direct nonconflicting production-branch change during the run can be merged and deployed even though it was absent from the staged build, while both recorded approvals still name the same unchanged release tip; the owner and app users receive untested/unapproved combined code.
findings.text: Phase7 and A10 bind staging/production approval to the release tip alone, but an unchanged release tip does not prove that finishing into a moved production target deploys the staged code. At read_dev, git.line_finish checks the recorded line head and mergeability; a nonconflicting target-only commit survives the merge without changing that head. Extend the private release runbook and A10 evidence to capture the target tip and actual promotion candidate tree/artifact alongside the staged identity. Re-evaluate before the irreversible promotion whenever either relevant tip changes; if equality to accepted staging is lost or unproven, stop and re-stage/re-obtain the separate owner approvals rather than treating the unchanged release head as sufficient. Clarify that external staging evidence becoming stale is a root procedure, not an automatic engine guarantee. This needs no app/engine deploy-flow redesign or new privacy machinery.

output.summary: Approved: Phase 7 and A10 resolve the production-target/candidate evidence gap while preserving separate owner approvals and the existing deployment boundary.

output.summary: Revised the private-app dogfood plan to bind staging and production decisions to the release tip, production target tip and resulting promotion candidate tree/artifact. The root rechecks that proof immediately before irreversible promotion and after waits/retries; relevant changes or unproven equality require a stop, restaging and renewed separate owner approvals. OD1–OD8, actual-actor attribution, privacy and the existing engine/app deployment boundaries are preserved.

Consolidated review approves all seven applied lenses; Adversary identifies one material release-evidence gap that reopens design. Equal release tips do not bind a moving production target or prove the promoted candidate equals accepted staging. Phase7/A10 and the private runbook must capture/recheck target and candidate identity, stop when equality is lost or unproven, and renew staging/separate owner approvals as needed. This implements OD3/OD6 procedurally without engine/deploy redesign. No non-material notes:0; verdicts are empty because material findings reopen automatically.

not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.
intent.purpose: Let coding agents carry long-running repository work through durable, reviewable goals, so a developer can stop supervising without losing progress, priorities or control.
intent.serves: Developers who delegate project work to coding agents, and the agents doing it.

output.summary: Approved corrected plan: staging and separate production decisions now bind both tips and the resulting candidate tree/artifact, with fresh proof before irreversible promotion and stop/restage/renewed approvals on movement or uncertainty. Root procedure is correctly distinguished from engine guarantees; OD1–OD8 remain intact.

Approved: generic immutable A1–A20 protocol covers the approved design and OD1–OD8, genuine matching-build two-harness work, actual migration/stack/release evidence, distinct same-tip staging/production approvals, recomputable costs and privacy boundaries. Future report/data stay editable; missing data remains intentional pre-run red. Two existing validators pass (0.034s). No findings; execution prerequisites and deploy authority remain separate.

spec:
The owner's direction (2026-11-01), verbatim: "whitepaper should be after dogfood run, we'll use the [private app, name redacted] repository as a dogfood test - migrate the goals and execute through to a release."

Dogfood the Release 1 engine end to end on the owner's private web application repository (its location is in the root's private notes), which still has a pre-reset ZzzOps installation (.zzzops/PROJECT.md, POLICY.json, proposals, portfolio caches) and old-style goal issues:
1. Install the plugin built from this repository's dev in both Claude Code and Codex (the owner: "We can update Codex for the dogfooding rather than wait for release"; Codex moves off the 15b59a5 copies at the start of this run, and both harnesses take part). Legacy detection (G1015) must show the migrate item; run the migrate-zzzops-repository skill and bootstrap: capture the private app's intent with the owner, write policy from the templates (the Release 1 consolidated graph, G1022), the template provenance record (G1024), required capabilities (G1027) and the branching block (G1025).
2. Migrate the private app's open goals into goal branches; close or record the ones that no longer apply, with the owner.
3. Execute through to a release: run the migrated goals through the default graph (design with owner questions raised by review (G1026), reviews, approvals, base, tests, implementation, CI, integrate, merge), including at least one stacked dependent and one goal that restacks after its dependency merges; then cut the release branch when every goal of the release is done, sync it to dev, and finish it into the production branch (G1025). Deploys, tags and CI stay the private app's own; the owner approves the finish because it may deploy.
4. Exercise the failure paths that occur naturally or that the root can trigger safely: a review finding that reopens its target, a failing check, an expired lease reclaimed from a second clone, a policy branch that pauses work.

Acceptance:
- Every migrated goal closes done (or is closed with the owner's reason) with no hand edits of zzzops/** refs beyond REPAIR.md recipes.
- One the private app release is cut, synced and finished through the engine.
- Every defect found is captured as its own goal in this repository, and the run's notes (what worked, what did not, cost per goal) are written up for the whitepaper (G1002).
- Re-score the consolidated review lenses on these real goals (G1022's follow-up).


Replaces G1003 and G1035, whose branches were deleted to remove private details of the owner's dogfood app (owner decision, 2026-11-01). Anonymity rule (owner): "Anonymised entirely"; nothing in this repository names the app. The detailed run plan and every app-specific fact live in the root's private journal outside this repository. Owner (2026-11-01): "I don't think we need to worry too much about scrubbing secrets, that's intent drift in my opinion.." So privacy is a convention: never name the app, keep public artifacts generic, replace identifying words in owner quotes with [redacted], and check the report and this goal's public artifacts for the app's name and repository slug once before publishing.
title: Dogfood Release 1 on a private web app repository: migrate its goals and execute through to a release
